anomalies.observed: C2 is a 100nF capacitor connected between the +5V rail and GND. The +5V rail is the output of U1, an LM1117-5.0 linear regulator.
anomalies.expected: The LM1117-5.0 datasheet requires a minimum output capacitance of 10µF (tantalum) for stability. A 100nF capacitor is insufficient and may cause the regulator to oscillate.

evidence.quote: C2 | 100nF | Capacitor_SMD:C_0805_2012Metric | Device:C_Small | Unpolarized capacitor, small symbol
+5V : C2.1(passive) J3.1(Pin_1,passive) J4.2(VCC,passive) J6.2(Pin_2,passive) R3.1(passive) U1.2(VO,power_out) U2.8(VCC,power_in) U3.8(VCC,power_in)

anomalies.impact: The 5V rail may oscillate or be unstable, affecting the MCU and other 5V components.

anomalies.observed: R6 (10K pull-up) is connected between VCC and TACH. R4 (1K series) is between TACH and /TACH_IN. D1 (5V1 Zener) is on TACH. The pull-up is therefore on the MCU side of the series resistor.
anomalies.expected: For an open-collector tach signal, the pull-up should be on the fan side of the series resistor (i.e., between VCC and /TACH_IN) so that when the fan pulls low, the MCU input is pulled to 0V through the series resistor. With the current arrangement, the MCU sees a voltage divider (VCC * 1K / (10K + 1K)) when the fan pulls low, which may not be a valid logic low for all VCC values.

anomalies.impact: The tach input may not read low correctly, causing unreliable fan speed measurement.

parsed.summary: The design contains two anomalies: the LM1117-5.0 output capacitor C2 is only 100nF instead of the required 10µF, risking regulator instability; and the tach input pull-up R6 is on the wrong side of the series resistor R4, degrading the logic low level seen by the MCU.
